about: The concept ladder (feature H11; docs/LEARNING.md §5): which chess ideas the coach names at each vocabulary level. 'use' is the column of the table in LEARNING: used constantly at about 500, introduced simply, or deferred. 'from' is the lowest vocabulary level (the setting coach.vocabulary: core, intro, all) at which the coach may use the word; below it the validator refuses the word unless the owner asked about it, and tells the coach to say the plain version instead. 'words' are regular expressions (case does not matter).

concepts.name: hanging or undefended piece
concepts.plain: a piece nothing protects

concepts.name: counting attackers and defenders
concepts.plain: how many pieces attack a square and how many protect it

concepts.name: checks, captures, threats
concepts.plain: the forcing moves to look at first

concepts.name: the opponent's threat
concepts.plain: what their last move wants to do next

concepts.name: piece values and trades
concepts.plain: what each piece is worth, and whether a swap is fair

concepts.name: back-rank and queen mates
concepts.plain: checkmate on the last rank; checkmate with the queen next to the king

concepts.name: fork
concepts.plain: one piece attacking two things at once

concepts.name: pin
concepts.plain: a piece that cannot move without exposing something more valuable behind it

concepts.name: skewer
concepts.plain: an attack on a valuable piece that must move, exposing the piece behind it

concepts.name: opening principles
concepts.plain: develop the pieces, control the centre, castle

concepts.name: king safety
concepts.plain: how exposed the king is

concepts.name: the piece that is doing nothing
concepts.plain: which of your pieces is not taking part yet

concepts.name: active and passive pieces
concepts.plain: a piece with many good squares against one with few

concepts.name: trade when ahead
concepts.plain: swap pieces when you have more material

concepts.name: outpost
concepts.plain: a square for your piece that their pawns can never attack

concepts.name: isolated pawn
concepts.plain: a pawn with no pawn of its own on the files beside it

concepts.name: good and bad bishop
concepts.plain: a bishop that is, or is not, blocked by its own pawns

concepts.name: pawn structure
concepts.plain: how the pawns are arranged, and what that lets each side do

concepts.name: space advantage
concepts.plain: more room for your pieces to move

concepts.name: intermezzo
concepts.plain: an in-between move, played before the expected recapture

concepts.name: fianchetto
concepts.plain: a bishop developed to the long diagonal, behind the knight's pawn

concepts.name: opposite-coloured bishops
concepts.plain: each side has one bishop, and they move on different colours

concepts.name: prophylaxis
concepts.plain: a move that stops their plan before it starts

concepts.name: minority attack
concepts.plain: pushing fewer pawns against more of theirs to make a weakness

concepts.name: isolani
concepts.plain: a queen's pawn with no pawns of its own beside it

concepts.name: imbalances
concepts.plain: the ways the two sides' positions differ

concepts.name: zugzwang
concepts.plain: a position where every move makes things worse

concepts.name: zwischenzug
concepts.plain: an in-between move, played before the expected recapture

concepts.name: weak colour complex
concepts.plain: a group of squares of one colour that cannot be defended
